text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-The Oil and Energy Department wants to allow the national auditor's office to inspect the books of North Sea oil companies in order to tighten control of exploration costs and other investments for which the government is partly billed by the companies.

-Three shooting incidents during the weekend have restarted a discussion on gun regulations. Lisbeth Holand, leader of parliament's justice committee, says the registration of weapons should improve and that illegal possession of weapons should be punished more strictly.
-A lack of energy and rising electricity prices has made it more interesting to build hydro-electric power plants. So far this year 10 power companies have sought permisson to build such plants.
-Norwegian conglomerate Orkla will most probably sell its brewery Hansa to investors for 320 million crowns.

-In 1995 people bought tax-free goods worth two billion crowns at Norwegian airports and ferries. Liquor is still the most popular buy, but its market share has decreased from 36.8 percent in 1992 to 32 percent in 1995.
